unit.why: A short anecdote, cited from another book, in which R. Pinhas of Korets cannot stop a baby's bleeding after a circumcision and R. Zusya of Hanipol stops it by ordering a festive meal.
unit.boundary_note: Part of a chain of quotations about circumcision and Elijah's chair; the previous and next divisions are separate teachings.

stories.start_quote: ע״פ מעשה המסופר מהה״ק ר״פ מקארץ
stories.end_quote: שבזה היה ממתיקין הדין ונעצר הדם
stories.summary_en: When R. Pinhas of Korets circumcised an infant and could not stop the bleeding, R. Zusya of Hanipol arrived, ordered a meal of eating and drinking, explained this by the verse 'they beheld God and ate and drank' as sweetening judgment, and the bleeding stopped.

quotes: שמל תינוק אחד ולא יכול לעצור הדם
tags.why: The story is set at a brit milah performed by R. Pinhas.
Uncontrolled bleeding in an infant is life-threatening, and the tsaddik's act ends the danger.

quotes: והנה כן היה שבזה היה ממתיקין הדין
tags.why: The bleeding stops miraculously through the meal.

quotes: ואמר כי כן כתיב ויחזו את האלהים ויאכלו וישתו
tags.why: Zusya explains his action through an exegesis of a verse.
Drinking at the meal is the means of the wonder, but wine is not named.
The tsaddik has the power to sweeten a judgment on another person's behalf.

quotes: כאשר ראו בחינות אלהים מד״הד שולט
tags.why: Protection from the attribute of strict judgment that rules at that moment.

missing_concepts: sweetening of judgments (המתקת הדינים) through a festive meal
quotation of the story from another book
